Agenda and accompanying board packet for the Troy School District regular Board of Education meeting held Tuesday, March 2, 2010, at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Recognition: The centerpiece is a resolution recognizing State Senator John Pappageorge and State Representative Marty Knollenberg. The narrative recounts that on October 19, 2009 Governor Granholm signed a school aid bill containing a line-item veto of 20j funding for the Troy School District and students in 40 other Michigan communities, arbitrarily cutting funding to Troy students by nearly $3 million annually, or $248.18 per pupil, beyond reductions already targeted to every Michigan district. The resolution states this veto broke a promise made to Troy voters as part of Proposal A in 1994 that their community would be held harmless in efforts to address school funding inequities. It recognizes both legislators for authoring and voting for measures to return the funds and for continuing to advocate in Lansing for reinstatement. The board extends its sincere appreciation and further resolves to urge both legislators to vote against any school aid bill that does not include full reinstatement of 20j revenue for Troy and other 20j communities. Signed the second day of March, 2010, with AYES/NAYS lines for adoption.

General Consent Agenda: approval of (A) minutes of the February 3, 2010 Board of Education meeting; (B) minutes of the February 9, 2010 Board of Education workshop; and (C) Awarding of Bid for Copy Paper, to be adopted together by resolution.

Curriculum: (A) REPORT on English Textbook Recommendation for Grades 6-12; (B) REPORT on the READ 180 Presentation.

Business: A series of considerations and reports — (A) CONSIDERATION of Artificial Turf Replacement; (B) CONSIDERATION of Tennis Court Updates; (C) CONSIDERATION of Smartboards; (D) CONSIDERATION of an Addendum to the Food Service Contract; (E) CONSIDERATION of Unfunded Mandates; (F) REPORT on the Budget Reduction Plan for the 2010/2011 School Year; and (G) CONSIDERATION of Authorization to Implement the Budget Reduction Plan. The meeting closes with Other and Adjournment. Vote tallies for the individual business items are not recorded in the extracted agenda text.

Meetings were cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

Background provided in the packet: the State Legislature had included language in the Michigan Department of Education budget that prohibits the use of state funds to implement or support the Common Core State Standards (CCSS) unless the Legislature takes specific action to support the standards. A subcommittee had been formed to study and make recommendations for Michigan's role in the CCSS initiative, and school boards were being asked to adopt a resolution in support of the CCSS.

The board adopted the resolution titled "Resolution Urging Continued Implementation And Funding Of the Common Core State Standards." It was moved by Ida Edmunds and supported by Gary Hauff, and passed by a vote of 7 YES to 0 NO. The resolution's whereas clauses state that education standards define expectations of what students should know but do not dictate curriculum or a particular method of instruction; that consistent standards provide appropriate benchmarks for all students regardless of where they live; that the CCSS were developed by states, for states, to provide clear K-12 expectations in English/language arts and mathematics leading to career- and college-readiness; that the standards promote equity, emphasize real-world skills and critical thinking, maintain local control of curriculum and teaching methods, and let districts continue to control textbooks and instructional methods. It further recites that the Michigan State Board of Education voted unanimously on June 15, 2010 to adopt the CCSS as the Michigan Core Standards for mathematics and English/language arts; that the Legislature inserted budget language effectively prohibiting Michigan from participating in the CCSS; that failure to implement would jeopardize Michigan's waiver under the No Child Left Behind Act and cause a majority of districts to fall below adequate yearly progress; and that abandoning implementation would confuse teachers and students. The resolving clause endorses the principles and goals of the CCSS and strongly urges the Michigan Legislature to support and fund their continued implementation. The resolution was passed and approved on the 21st day of August, 2013, and signed by Nancy Philippart, Board President, and Paula Fleming, Board Secretary.

The bulk of the document is a presentation on the district's Operations Research course, delivered by Kris Karbon and Carol Machak. The presentation framed three guiding questions: what the goals of the Operations Research class are, how it fits into the Troy School District's mathematics curriculum, and what kinds of problems students work on. Enrollment grew from 2 sections of Operations Research at Athens High School in 2012-13 to 4 sections in 2013-14.

To illustrate the coursework, the presentation walked through a decision-analysis problem titled "Which Sport Should Lauren Mitchell Play?" Students weighed criteria grouped under Cost (cost per session, equipment/uniform cost), Commitment (hours per week for practice/games, number of games), Enjoyment (group or individual, lifelong sport, enthusiasm to play), and Safety (potential for injury, long-term negative effects). These were classified as continuous measures (participation cost, equipment cost, hours for practice, number of games, enthusiasm, potential for injury) and categorical measures (group or individual, lifelong sport, long-term negative effects), each with a defined scoring method (for example, participation cost measured proportionally from $25 to $500; injuries per 1,000 participants scored proportionally from 1 to 20; group scored 1 and individual 0). A data table compared sports including soccer (participation cost $75.00, equipment $60.00, 3 hours/week, 10 games, group, enthusiasm 6, not lifelong, injury 16.4, moderate long-term effects), dance ($150.00 / $120.00 / 2 hours / 2 games / group / enthusiasm 9 / high), gymnastics ($380.00 / $25.00 / 3.5 hours / 6 games / individual / enthusiasm 10 / high), swimming ($250.00 / $40.00 / 4 hours / 6 games / group / enthusiasm 2 / lifelong / injury 6.5 / low), tennis ($250.00 / $35.00 / 3 hours / 8 games / individual / enthusiasm 7 / lifelong / injury 9.8 / moderate), and basketball.

Needa Toofanny is identified as a student at the International Academy - East.

Under Personnel (item 6), the board took up an Elementary and Secondary personnel consideration and a Negotiations Update report. Under Curriculum (item 7): (A) Consideration of the Sex Education Advisory Board for 2013-2014; (B) a Report on Professional Development for the 2013-2014 School Year; and (C) a Report on Advanced Placement Scholars. The Closed Session (item 11) was called for Negotiations and Attorney-Client Privilege.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Agenda and Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) materials for a Special Meeting of the Board of Trustees of the Troy School District, held October 15, 2013, beginning at 5:00 p.m. in the Administration Building at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The brief agenda comprised: (1) Pledge of Allegiance; (2) Public Communication; (3) Other, containing the substantive item; (4) Closed Session; and (5) Adjournment.

The core matter (item 3A) was consideration of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program (WOT). The document explains that WOT is an organization whose mission is to inspire, motivate, and empower at-risk young women to live up to their full potential through a unique mentoring program pairing them with highly accomplished professional women and offering scholarship opportunities. For Troy students to participate, the board was required to enter into the agreement by signing the MOU, and the recommended action was to adopt a resolution authorizing that signature.

The MOU identifies the two contracting parties: the Troy School Board (the School Board), whose address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; and the Women of Tomorrow Mentor & Scholarship Program, Detroit Metropolitan Area, Inc. (WOT-Metro Detroit), whose address is 17251 West 12 Mile Road, Suite 204, Southfield, MI 48076, or any affiliated entity thereof. The agreement was entered on the 15th day of October, 2013, to implement the WOT program commencing in October 2013.

The recitals state that both WOT and the School Board believe the program benefits Troy School District students; that the program is specifically designed to meet the needs of at-risk teenage girls in the nation's public high schools and to help them turn obstacles into opportunities by providing exposure, motivation, confidence, and opportunity; and that the program was founded and is headed by Jennifer Valoppi, an author and television journalist, in which a group of highly accomplished professional women serve as mentors to improve mentees' self-esteem, academic performance, high school graduation rate, and future adult prospects.

Following the WOT consideration, the board scheduled a Closed Session (item 4A) for Negotiations before adjournment. The document carries the district's standard public-participation notice (half-hour comment periods for agenda and non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker) and the usual cablecast/streaming information.
